mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 2.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 2.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when GDPC1 YoY change < -2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 8% for three consecutive months signals persistent labor market weakness, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profitability, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when UNRATE > 8% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals contraction in the manufacturing sector, which reduces earnings for industrial firms and drags on the S&P 500 over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during INDPRO declines for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (inflation) above their respective 5-year averages signals a stagflation risk, which increases uncertainty and discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 5-year averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A strong and persistent increase in housing starts (HOUST) above a 12-month moving average by more than 10% for two months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and supports broader market returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during periods when HOUST exceeds its 12-month moving average by more than 10% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous fall in both PAYEMS and UNRATE (payroll employment and unemployment rate) where PAYEMS declines while UNRATE rises signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS falls AND UNRATE rises in same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) when PAYEMS falls and UNRATE rises in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (proxied by RSAFS) above its 5-year average for three consecutive months signals elevated precautionary savings, which reduces near-term consumption and corporate revenue, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when RSAFS is above its 5-year average for three consecutive months.
